text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- a few hours after Commerce Minister M'Mkundia reiterates that Nakumatt supermarket will remain closed as its appeal is considered, statement from ministry official reinstates trade licence cancelled.
- President Moi orders Kenya African National Union party leaders to stop wrangling and resolve differences away from media spotlight.
- National carrier Kenya Airways wins 1996 World Bank award for excellence.
- Outgoing electoral commission chairman Justice Chesoni is at centre of accusations of bias by ruling KANU party members and opposition over creation of 22 new constituencies.

- Opposition parliament member Njenga Mungai tells Minister for Local Government Ntimama that any attempt to force non-Maasai and Kalenjins in Rift Valley into KANU party will be met with equal and powerful force.
- Industrial Development Bank chairman Chesire tells Kenya Dairy Board and politicians to stop interfering with management of giant milk Kenya Cooperative Creameries.
- Eldoret International Airport, to be operational by early next year, will be major boost to Western Kenya tourist circuit and other East African tourist destinations.
